 Critic's Review User Reviews Party Animals Movie Review: A vibrant but uneven comedy that doesn't quite hit the mark 
 Dhaval Roy TNN, Nov 19, 2026, 3:00 PM IST 2.5 /5 
 Story: Mann Patel ( Viraj Ghelani ) organises his first New Year's Eve bash and invites his childhood best friend, Armaan Khanna ( Arjun Tanwar ), who’s a budding actor and star kid. Their reunion begins as a fun night but soon descends into chaos with romantic drama, cops, and a gangster. Review: Director Ravi Chhabria’s romantic comedy opens at a convent school, where a young Armaan takes over the PA system to ask Simran to be his girlfriend. His wingman is his street-smart best buddy, Mann. Fast forward 15 years, and Mann is a loud Gujarati boy, while Armaan has grown into a hunky actor. The story follows the duo as they reunite for a party where romantic entanglements unfold and chaos ensues. Written by Ali Haji, Khush Mullick and Veer Panchal, the film’s premise has potential, but falters at the execution level. The narrative is overpacked with subplots and lacks focus throughout. There’s the story of an emotionally abusive and haughty superstar, Raj Khanna (Samir Soni), who is too hard on his son, Armaan, who strives to please his dad while longing for his childhood sweetheart, Simran (Jaanya Joshi). Mann tries to woo Saakshi (Naqiyah Haji), while his best friend Zahra (Pragati Nagpal) harbours romantic feelings for him. New Year’s Eve brings them all together at the bash, but Mann’s jealous rival, a fellow party organiser, sabotages the evening. A heartbroken Armaan’s idea of ‘moving on’ is to lock lips with Saakshi, while Mann gets back at him by seeking help from a gangster, Shakeel Bhai (Anil Charanjeett). Although the movie’s runtime is a modest 133 minutes, it feels longer as scenes drag on. Some one-liners and comic moments land and elicit laughter, but these remain few and far between. A drunk horse named Munna, who vocalises like Sanjay Dutt , and Shakeel Bhai and his stepbrother Ishteyaq (Aryan Prajapati) playing ‘goodminton’ with table tennis bats feel over the top. Emotional moments, such as Mann and Armaan drifting apart, the former longing to rekindle their friendship and the latter feeling stifled under his father’s shadow, could have been more impactful but feel flat. Cinematographer Karan Tanwar captures the party scenes effectively, lending the movie a contemporary look. Music remains one of its strong suits, with foot-tapping numbers such as Sunny Jandu’s Sheeshe Vibrate and Junior’s Cha Cha Cha Party . Content creator Viraj Ghelani, as the leading man Mann, delivers a confident and effortless performance. Arjun Tanwar is decent as Armaan, though his character could have benefited from a more focused track. Naqiyah Haji, Pragati Nagpal and Soundous Moufakir, as Armaan’s leading lady Kimaya, make their presence felt with their performances and screen presence. Saqib Ayub, Alam Khan , Anil Charanjeett, Kamlesh Sawant and Vijay Patkar lend able support, while Samir Soni makes an impact in his cameo. Party Animals has its moments, but the uneven storytelling keeps it from being the breezy, entertaining romantic comedy it sets out to be. Videos
